# 27 new spells — design guide, data sheet and build order

**Written:** 2026-09-04 · **Status:** mechanics IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-04 — all 8 systems, all 27
spells. **The LOOK specified in Part 3 largely did not ship.**

**Audited 2026-09-05 — mean 3.04 / 10 across the 27. See
[`SPELL_VISUAL_AUDIT_AND_ROADMAP.md`](SPELL_VISUAL_AUDIT_AND_ROADMAP.md).** Every "**Look.**"
paragraph below is binding specification and most of them were not built: 24 of 27 spells
share one of four generic rigs, six draw nothing at all in flight, and the worst-scoring axis
is Law L1 — the law this document opens by calling the single most repeated mistake in the
codebase. Read the audit before treating any spell below as finished.

> **Implementation notes.** Every system in Part 2 shipped, and all 27 spell assets plus their
> 71 grimoire nodes are generated by `Valkur > Spells > Seed Expansion Spells` followed by
> `Valkur > Progression > Seed Progression Content`. Three things came out differently from the
> plan and the differences are recorded where they happened rather than smoothed over here:
>
> - **S8 turned out smaller than budgeted and S5 turned out to hide a defect.** The allied
>   summon needed one helper (`FactionTargeting.EnemyOf`) and a mechanical substitution across
>   twenty call sites, not a forked FSM set. Meanwhile `AuraExecutor` was found dividing
>   `radius` by 16 — the SIXTH Python-pixel sighting — which survived only because
>   `InitializeHealing` discarded the value it was handed.
> - **`TotemController` healed exactly one entity**, its owner, so S4 was not "add a sweep" but
>   "the area this spell draws has never existed".
> - **The per-facet cracking described for `guardian_light` is NOT implemented.** The absorb
>   pool, the early break and the ripple-scaled-by-remaining-pool are; the shell does not yet
>   accumulate visible cracks as it drains. That is a deliberate deferral, not an oversight —
>   see the note at the end of this document.
>
> Node ordering inside a school is insertion order, so the new nodes sit after the old ones
> rather than in level order. `SpellNode.row` is layout only and the prerequisite chain is
> correct; sorting the view is a HUD concern.

## What this document is

The complete brief for growing Valkur's grimoire from **46 player-castable spells to 73**,
on the way to a stated target of roughly 100. It is written to be handed to an implementing
session as-is: every spell below carries its authored data, its visual specification and an
honest cost, and every shared system a spell depends on is named and ordered.

Read it in this order:

1. **The laws** — the VFX rules this project has already paid for. Breaking one of them is
   how a spell ends up invisible, washed out, or drawing under the wall tops. They are not
   style preferences; each was measured.
2. **The eight systems** — what has to be built before the data means anything. Eleven of
   the 27 are pure data today. Sixteen are not, and this section says exactly why.
3. **The 27** — per school, with full field values.
4. **The contract** — units, gotchas and the tests that must go green.

## Two decisions that shape everything below

**Spells go into the nine EXISTING schools, not into new functional categories.** The
arithmetic settles it: at 100 spells, nine schools give ~11 nodes per tab, which reads as a
list. Seven functional categories would give damage ~45 and leave six tabs nearly empty.

The cost of that choice is that FUNCTION becomes invisible — a player looking for "what
heals me" has to already know that healing lives in Radiance. The fix is one field, and it
belongs in this work rather than after it: **`SpellNode.role`**, a small enum
(`Damage, Control, Protection, Healing, Mobility, Summon, Utility`) plus a filter row in the
grimoire HUD. Structure by school, search by role. Adding it at 71 nodes is trivial; adding
it at 100 means re-tagging by hand.

**The 27 also rebalance the schools**, which are badly lopsided today — Cryomancy has 2
nodes against Arcana's 8:

| School | Today | New | After |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Cryomancy | 2 | +5 | 7 |
| Verdant Rites | 3 | +5 | 8 |
| Umbramancy | 4 | +4 | 8 |
| Radiance | 5 | +4 | 9 |
| Stormcalling | 4 | +3 | 7 |
| Martial Forms | 5 | +3 | 8 |
| Pyromancy | 6 | +2 | 8 |
| Arcana | 8 | +1 | 9 |
| Inner Fire | 7 | +0 | 7 |
| **Total** | **44** | **+27** | **71** |

Plus the two innate spells (`slash_regular`, `weapon_toggle`) = 73 castable.

---

# Part 1 — The laws

Every rule here was paid for once already, in a defect that shipped. They are listed first
because a spell that breaks one of them does not look *slightly* worse — it looks broken, or
it looks like nothing at all. The full history behind each is in `CLAUDE.md`; this is the
operating version.

## L1. The rig must be shaped like the thing it draws

Recorded three times. A `LineRenderer` cannot draw a cone (it is a wire outline — a strip can
bound a shape and never fill one, which is why the flame breath's entire silhouette was two
strokes and a curve). A radial disc rig cannot draw a line (`AreaFXRig` stretched onto the ice
wall turned four discs into ellipses and put the emitter at a point in the middle). A radial
disc cannot draw a funnel either: it can never show the one thing a vortex is named after,
its rotation.

**So:** before writing a single constant, name the SILHOUETTE. Column, line, wedge, sphere,
ring, funnel, column-of-falling-things. Then build the rig from that shape outward. Reaching
for `AreaFXRig` because it is convenient is the single most repeated mistake in this codebase.

## L2. On an additive material, alpha is COVERAGE and colour is BRIGHTNESS

`ElementalSprites.SharedAdditiveMaterial` and `ParticleMaterialCache.Get(tex, additive: true)`
are both `SrcAlpha/One`. Consequences, all measured:

- **To make an effect fiercer, raise the COLOUR, not the alpha.** `SpriteRenderer.color`
  accepts values above 1 (an authored `2.400` reads back unchanged, and both `Camera.allowHDR`
  and the URP asset's `supportsHDR` are on, so the excess reaches the framebuffer). Raising the
  alpha instead WIDENS the effect into fog rather than hardening it.
- **A "dark" effect is authored by darkening the colour and leaving the alpha alone.** A deep
  indigo at alpha 0.85 still covers the whole silhouette; it just adds dark violet light.
  Lowering the alpha makes it FAINT, which is a different thing and usually the wrong one.
- **Particles are the exception to the overdrive.** A particle's vertex colour packs to
  `Color32` and CLAMPS at 1. Get a particle layer's intensity from SATURATION instead.
- **The layer COUNT is a brightness dial.** Raising `VortexFunnelFX.BANDS` from 9 to 18 took
  the summed band alpha from 3.99 to 7.97 and washed a red vortex white through its own middle.
  Divide per-layer alpha by a reference count so more layers buy RESOLUTION, not light. Above a
  summed alpha of about 3 the centre is flat white and the spell stops being distinguishable
  from any other spell.
- **Thickness is a brightness dial too**, for the same reason: doubling a band's weight doubles
  the screen area it covers. Compensate.

## L3. One opaque layer is what separates "affecting the world" from "lit"

Every other layer of a good rig is additive light. Exactly one — ground debris, torn-up chips,
scattered soil — should be `Sprite-Unlit-Default` and deliberately DARK. It cannot be folded
into the shared additive material as a tidy-up: a dark chip on an additive surface adds almost
nothing, so the layer would vanish with nothing failing. `KiAuraFX` and `VortexFunnelFX` both
record this; `VortexFieldTests` pins the material contrast in both directions.

## L4. An effect made only of continuous motion stops being read after about a second

Bands turning, particles streaming, streaks running — all at a steady rate — and the eye files
the whole thing as one texture. What resets attention is an EVENT: something appears and is
gone. The duty cycle is the entire design. `VortexFunnelFX`'s first discharge interval measured
**78 % of frames lit**, which is not lightning but a lamp with a flicker. Shipped at 0.45–1.30 s
between strikes: **30 % duty**, six or seven distinct events per two-second cast.

**Target roughly 30 % duty for any event layer.** Above 50 % it is a texture again.

## L5. Identity root, absolute child sizes

A rig that wants a world size gives its children ABSOLUTE sizes and leaves its root at
identity. Scaling the root scales every child TWICE if they were already sized, and — worse —
scales any `Light2D` parented under it. The vortex's light rendered at an effective **367 world
units**, eleven screen widths of violet, from exactly this. `PuddleController` and
`TotemController` still carry the same two lines; their radii are small enough that it has not
surfaced yet. Do not copy them.

## L6. Sorting is a layer plus a small order, and index-derived orders need a derived bound

- World-space effects go on `LAYER_VFX` with a small order. `SortingConfig.Z_SKY` is a **Z
  depth, not a sorting order** — passing it as `sortingOrder` on the Entities layer drew every
  lightning bolt under the wall tops. Recorded twice (`LightningBoltFX`, then
  `ElementalProjectileVisual`).
- If layer `i` gets order `BASE + i`, anything that must draw in front of the whole stack needs
  `BASE + COUNT + n`, computed, never a literal. A hand-typed `ORDER_DUST = 72` was correct at
  9 bands and silently wrong at 18.
- A rig sorted against its CASTER must rebase every frame: `YSortEntity` rewrites the caster's
  order whenever they walk, and a value captured at build time pops the effect in front of the
  character the first time they take a step.

## L7. A ground-plane layer is squashed by ONE parent, never per item

A radial streak squashed individually is foreshortened in LENGTH without being turned, so it
slides across the floor instead of lying on it. One `GroundPlane` transform at roughly
`(1, 0.34, 1)`, with the per-item rotation on the CHILDREN of that squash.

Related: **a sprite parent may only ever be turned about Z** — a `LookRotation` on a sprite
puts its quad edge-on to the camera and it vanishes, invisible rather than wrong-looking, the
failure nobody reports. Meanwhile **a `ParticleSystem`'s Cone shape emits along its own +Z and
needs exactly that `LookRotation`**. One transform cannot be both: carry two oriented children
under one identity root.

And never hand-derive a 2D aim as `Quaternion.Euler`. A `Euler(deg - 90, 90, 0)` is a MIRROR
about the 45 degree diagonal, and it shipped: six of eight facings sprayed the fire somewhere
other than the damage, and only the diagonals tested clean.
`Quaternion.LookRotation(dir, Vector3.forward)` is exact on all eight.

## L8. Every `ElementalSprites` sprite is exactly 1x1 world unit

`Sprite.Create` is handed the texture size as `pixelsPerUnit` for all eleven, so a 128 px Halo
is no bigger in world than a 32 px HotCore — resolution buys detail, not extent. **A scale
constant IS a world diameter.**

`Ring`'s bright band peaks at normalized radius **0.78**, which makes a drawn boundary pinnable
to a damage radius at any size: `ringScale = radius / 0.39`. Getting this wrong is invisible in
code and brutal on screen — the arcane flame's only hard contour sat at 1.511 u against a
2.5 u damage circle, so 46 % of the area that hurt carried no readable pixel.

**The silhouette must promise what the damage delivers.** Where the shape a player reads is not
the shape that hurts — a funnel is widest metres above the ground circle it queries — something
else, normally a pinned ground ring, has to state the real reach.

## L9. Colour and gesture are two axes

`ElementPalette` answers "what element is this". `CastFlourishProfile` answers "what is the
caster DOING". They are genuinely orthogonal: an ice wall and an ice bolt are the same blue and
nothing like the same gesture. Nine gesture families exist and are dispatched off `SpellType`
automatically:

| Family | Gesture | Reached by |
|---|---|---|
| Hurl | spirals in, throws forward | Projectile, Boomerang, default |
| Edge | strikes sparks off the swing arc, draws no circle | Slash |
| Conjure | circle EXPANDS while motes fall from the sky | Area, Wall, Trap, Mine, Puddle, Totem, Summon, Smoke, SmokeEmitter, ArcaneFlame |
| Invoke | lifts motes off the floor and throws them at the sky | Meteor, Lightning, ChainLightning, FireworkLaunch |
| Ward | orbits the body and never lets go | Aura, Shield, SphereMagicShield |
| Surge | leaves its motes BEHIND | Dash |
| Vanish | implodes, no burst, no lance | Teleport |
| Channel | breathes and holds | Beam, ConeBreath |
| Vortex | a silhouette rather than points of light | VortexField |

Every new spell inherits its family from its `SpellType` for free. Check the family it lands in
is the gesture you meant; if it is not, that is usually a sign the `SpellType` is wrong. A new
`SpellType` must be added to that switch or it silently falls through to Hurl.

## L10. `particleColor` has three meanings and they must be tested in this order

1. **Opaque white is the "nobody authored this" sentinel** (`KiPalette.IsUnauthored`). Such a
   spell correctly keeps its ELEMENT's colour.
2. **An achromatic non-white value is a deliberate request for the ABSENCE of colour** and must
   desaturate. `RGBToHSV` reports hue 0 for grey, and hue 0 is RED — a naive blend lit a grey
   blade with a pale pink gather.
3. **Near-black adds nothing on an additive material.** A flourish derived from a 0.04 grey
   would not dim, it would disappear. `ElementPalette.RecolouredTo` moves the HUE and keeps
   each field's own VALUE and ALPHA, because that spread is what makes a flourish read as a hot
   centre inside a soft bloom rather than as six sprites of one colour.

**Author `particleColor` on every one of the 27.** Ten shipped spells still leave it white, and
that is a defect rather than a default.

## L11. Author in WORLD UNITS

Recorded **five** times: `wallWidth`/`wallHeight`, the totem's radius, the vortex's radius,
`coneLength` and `arcane_flame`'s radius were all authored in the pixel scale of the Python
build this game was ported from, with a `/16` or `/32` hiding in the executor. Every one was
internally consistent and disagreed only with the screen. The tell is always the same: **the
executor's fallback for an unauthored field is many times larger than anything the asset can
produce.**

Scale reference — the camera is 33.33 x 16.67 world units, a character is about 1.86 u tall, a
spell that reads as "big" is 3-4 u, and anything past 8 u fills the screen.

## L12. Intensity is DENSITY and BEHAVIOUR, not size

The seven shipped ki charges run 0.15 to 1.00 on `scale`, and what that dial moves is 6 to 15
flame tongues, 35 to 130 sparks a second, no ground debris at all below 0.32, no lightning
below 0.60, ring pulses every 2.1 s down to every 0.34 s. HEIGHT barely moves (3.5 to 4.5 u),
because a calm charge should read as CALM, not as small. The first heights tried put the void
charge at 9.8 u against a 10 u-tall camera and it stopped reading as something coming off a
person.

## L13. Five smaller traps that cost a day each

- **`main.duration` cannot be written while a ParticleSystem is playing.** `AddComponent` starts
  it immediately. Order is `Stop(true, StopEmittingAndClear)`, configure, `Play()`.
- **`velocityOverLifetime` axes must all be in the same curve mode**, or Unity logs once per
  frame per system. And a **Box shape emits along its own FORWARD**, which in a 2D scene is
  into the screen, so `startSpeed` on a box buys motion nobody can see.
- **Reparenting during `OnEnable`/`OnDisable` is silently refused.** Defer the attach to the
  next `LateUpdate`.
- **`Sprite-Unlit-Default` declares no `_SrcBlend`/`_DstBlend`**, so every blend-mode write
  against it is a silent no-op. Use the two correct additive paths, and remember a material
  handed to a `ParticleSystemRenderer` must carry its OWN texture or it draws white squares.
- **A persistent effect has five exit paths and only `OnDestroy` is on all of them** — its own
  timer, eviction by `maxInstances`, a zone change, the caster dying, scene unload. A fade the
  effect implements on its own timeline is simply skipped. Implement `ISpellEffectDissipates`.

## L14. A spell's light is not a world fixture

Do not subscribe a spell's `Light2D` to `DayNightCycle.OnLightsEnabledChanged`. A torch should
only burn at night; a spell should be lit whenever it is cast. `ArcaneFlameController` did this
and was the only one of eleven light-carrying spell controllers that went dark at noon — for
most of a session, and the light is the half of that rig that says the ground is dangerous.

## L15. The report of a distant effect arrives AFTER its picture

`0.020 s per world unit travelled`. It costs one float and it is most of what makes a burst
read as happening out there rather than on the lens. Its sibling is the anticipation cue: a
rising whistle during a flight is what makes a player LOOK UP, so the burst lands on an eye
already pointed at it.

# Part 2 — The eight systems

Eleven of the 27 are pure data against an executor that already exists. The other sixteen
are not, and the honest reason is that several of the engine's spell verbs are thinner than
their names suggest. Three of them were measured while writing this document and the finding
changed the plan:

- **`SummonExecutor` produces no creature.** It builds a GameObject with a `SpriteRenderer`, a
  `Rigidbody2D`, a `CircleCollider2D`, `Health.Initialize(50)` and a `SummonController` despawn
  timer. No FSM brain, no `MeleeCombat`, no target acquisition. `CreateSummonSprite()` generates
  a plain white circle. `summon_barbol` is a green blob that stands still and can be killed.
- **`TotemController.HealTick()` heals only the OWNER.** It does
  `_owner.GetComponent<Health>()` and heals that one entity. There is no radius sweep and no
  notion of an ally. `healing_totem` is a stationary self-heal with a decorative pole.
- **`SpellType.Trap` (8) and `SpellType.Shield` (9) are not in the dispatch table.** They fall
  through to `ProjectileExecutor` with a warning. `ShieldExecutor` is wired to
  `SphereMagicShield` (18) instead. Do not author a spell against either of the two dead values.

Build the systems in the order below. Each row says what it unlocks, so an early stop still
ships whole spells rather than half of everything.

| # | System | Unlocks | Size |
|---|---|---|---:|
| S0 | `SpellNode.role` + grimoire filter | navigation for all 73 | XS |
| S1 | `BuffExecutor` + `SpellDefinition.statModifiers` | 4 spells | S |
| S2 | Projectile mechanics: pierce, homing, volley | 4 spells + retrofit | M |
| S3 | Charged cast | 1 spell now, any spell later | M |
| S4 | Area-effect totem | 1 spell | S |
| S5 | Damaging aura | 1 spell | S |
| S6 | Absorb shield (HP pool, not an invincible flag) | 1 spell | M |
| S7 | Enemy debuff layer | 1 spell | M |
| S8 | Allied summon (FSM + faction) | 2 spells | **L** |

## S0 — `SpellNode.role`

A `SpellRole` enum on `SpellNode` (`Damage, Control, Protection, Healing, Mobility, Summon,
Utility`) plus a filter row in the grimoire HUD. Do it first: it is a field and a chip strip,
and every node authored after it exists gets tagged as it is written rather than in a
re-tagging pass at 100 spells.

## S1 — `BuffExecutor`

**The highest-leverage single piece of work in the list.** A new `SpellType.Buff` whose
executor reads a `StatModifier[]` off the SpellDefinition and hands it to
`TimedBuffSource.Apply(key, modifiers, duration)`, which already exists and already refreshes
rather than stacks on a repeated key.

New `SpellDefinition` fields: `statModifiers` (`StatModifier[]`) and `buffKey` (`string`, the
refresh key — default to `spellKey` when blank).

This turns the entire protection and support category into pure data, forever. Every future
"+X for Y seconds" spell in the run to 100 costs one asset.

Append `SpellType.Buff` to the enum (**never insert** — every shipped SpellDefinition stores
the enum as its integer) and add it to `CastFlourishProfile`'s switch under **Ward**, or it
falls through to Hurl and a self-buff throws motes forward at nothing.

## S2 — Projectile mechanics

Three independent flags on `SpellDefinition`, read by `ProjectileExecutor` and `Projectile`.
None of them needs a new `SpellType`, which is the point: any of the 12 existing projectile
spells can be given one later without new code.

| Field | Type | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pierceCount` | int | Enemies passed THROUGH before despawn. 0 = today's behaviour (stop at first). | 0 |
| `pierceDamageFalloff` | float | Fraction of damage lost per enemy pierced. | 0 |
| `homingStrength` | float | Turn rate in degrees/second toward the acquired target. 0 = straight. | 0 |
| `homingRange` | float | Acquisition radius in world units. | 0 |
| `projectileCount` | int | Shots fired per cast. | 1 |
| `spreadDegrees` | float | Total fan angle across `projectileCount`. | 0 |

Watch two traps recorded in `CLAUDE.md`. **`Projectile.range` defaults to 20** and silently
expired the boomerang's return leg and the firework's whole flight — author `range` on every
one of these. And **a damage radius is not a collision radius**: sweeping obstacles with a
generous `hitRadius` catches a piercing shot on scenery nobody aimed at. Sweep walls with the
collider, sweep enemies with `hitRadius`.

## S3 — Charged cast

Hold the key to charge; release to fire. Damage, size and — where it makes sense — the number
of projectiles scale with hold time.

**Build it as a MODIFIER, not as one spell.** New `SpellDefinition` fields
`chargeMaxSeconds`, `chargeDamageMultiplier`, `chargeScaleMultiplier`, `chargeMinFraction`,
plus a `ChargedCastController` that holds the cast open while the key is down and multiplies
the resolved values on release. `channelDuration` already exists but nothing reads HOLD TIME to
scale anything, which is why this is real work rather than a field.

It costs more now and it is the only item on this list that gets cheaper with every spell
added afterwards: at 100 spells, "this one is chargeable" should be a bool.

The charge itself is a visual opportunity and must be one — see `charged_bolt` in Part 3.

## S4 — Area-effect totem

`TotemController` gains a radius sweep that heals every friendly entity inside it rather than
only `_owner`. While in there, fix `CLAUDE.md`'s L5 violation: the controller currently does
`AreaFXRig.Attach(...)` and then `transform.localScale = Vector3.one * radius`, sizing every
child twice and scaling the `Light2D` with it.

"Friendly" needs an answer, and the cheapest correct one is a tag/layer test rather than a new
faction system: heal the caster plus anything on the Player layer.

## S5 — Damaging aura

`AuraRegistry` holds exactly two auras today (`toughness`, `manaflow`), both of which are stat
buffs on the caster. A damaging aura is a new registry entry with a periodic
`Physics2D.OverlapCircleAll` against the NPC layer.

## S6 — Absorb shield

The existing shield is a boolean `SetInvincible`, which is binary and unreadable — nothing on
screen can express "two more hits". An absorb shield holds an HP pool, drains it on each blow
and breaks with an event.

**`SetInvincible` has three independent owners** (the dev console's god mode, the F4 editor's
test invulnerability, and the shield) so it must be SAVED AND RESTORED, never cleared — and the
`SpellEffectRegistry.Track` call that evicts a previous shield has to happen BEFORE the new
controller claims the flag, or the sequence runs backwards and two spheres leave the player
mortal. Both defects shipped once.

`Health.OnDamageBlocked` already exists and fires only for a blow that was genuinely turned
away. Drive the absorb ripple off it.

## S7 — Enemy debuff layer

The layered stat store is a player system: `PlayerStats` with its seven layers hangs off the
player. An NPC has `EntityStats` and no equivalent. A curse that makes a target take more
damage needs either a minimal per-entity modifier list read by `Health.MitigateDamage`, or a
status effect carrying a multiplier.

**Prefer the status-effect route.** `StatusEffectManager` already owns application, duration,
refresh, immunities and the `SpriteTintStack` layer, and a new `VulnerableEffect` inherits all
of it. Building a second stat store on the NPC side is how the project ends up with two
composition rules that disagree.

## S8 — Allied summon

The big one, and the reason two spells sit at the bottom of the build order.

A real summon reuses the monster pipeline — `MonsterDefinition` plus
`EntitySetup.ConfigureMonster` plus `FSMMonsterBrain` — with the target selection inverted. The
obstacle is documented in `CLAUDE.md` and is not incidental: **no state class reads
`stats.faction`.** The only thing that makes a faction peaceful today is the FSM set's
allowed-state whitelist, so `NPC_Passive` is harmless purely because it declares no
`ChaseState`.

So an ally needs one of two things, and the choice should be made deliberately:

1. **A faction-aware target query.** `ChaseState` and `AttackState` ask a single helper "who is
   my enemy" instead of assuming the player. This is the correct long-term answer and it also
   unlocks monster-versus-monster fights, boss adds and charmed enemies.
2. **A dedicated `Monster_Ally` FSM set** whose states target the NPC layer. Cheaper, and it
   forks the state classes, which is the shape of problem this project has recorded eleven
   times under "authored and inert".

Recommend (1). It is a helper and two call sites, and it is the difference between "summons
work" and "summons work for these two spells".

# Part 3 — The 27

## How to read a spell entry

**Node** is the grimoire placement: school, arcane-point cost, level gate, prerequisite node,
`role` tag. **Needs** names the system from Part 2, or `free` when the executor already exists.
**Data** lists only the fields that differ from the asset default — everything unlisted stays
at its serialized default. **Look** is the visual specification, and it is binding: it names
the silhouette first, then the layer stack, because that is the order Law L1 demands.

Reference scale from the shipped catalog: mana 10-18, damage 10-40, cooldown 0.4-9 s, range
6-15 u, radius 1.7-2.8 u. The 27 are authored inside that band so they slot into the existing
economy without a global retune.

Names are neutral placeholders, as agreed — the personality pass comes after the mechanics
land, and renaming a `spellKey` after release breaks save persistence, so **the key is the
thing to get right now** even where the display name is provisional.

---

## Cryomancy — 2 nodes to 7

*"Not colder. Slower, until nothing moves at all."* Accent `(0.45, 0.78, 1.00)`.
Affinities: mague, elven. The school gets the largest share because it is the thinnest today
and because slow-and-hold is a complete identity that two spells cannot express.

### `frost_nova` — Frost Nova

**Node:** cryomancy · cost 1 · level 5 · prereq `iceball` · role Control
**Needs:** free — `AreaExecutor` is registered, applies damage and runs
`StatusApplicationFactory.ApplyAll`, and no player spell uses it yet.

A radial burst from the caster's feet. Small damage, real control: everything in the ring is
slowed, and a minority of targets freeze outright.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `Area` |
| `manaCost` / `cooldownDuration` | 14 / 6 |
| `damage` | 18 |
| `radius` | 3.2 |
| `element` | `Ice` |
| `particleColor` | `(0.62, 0.88, 1.00)` |
| `castAnchor` | `Feet` |
| `statusApplications` | `Slow` 3.0 s, magnitude 0.55, chance 1.0 · `Freeze` 1.2 s, chance 0.30 |

**Look.** Silhouette: a RING travelling outward across the floor, not a disc appearing. Six
layers. (1) A ground ring on `ElementalSprites.Ring`, scaled `radius / 0.39` so its bright band
lands exactly on 3.2 u — it starts at zero and expands to full over 0.18 s, which is the whole
statement about reach. (2) A low haze disc trailing 0.06 s behind the ring, additive, pale
cyan, fading from the centre outward so the middle empties as the wave leaves. (3) **Ice
spikes** — 14 `IceSprites.Facet` quads standing UP from the floor along the ring, each spawned
as the ring's radius passes its angle, so they erupt in sequence rather than all at once; that
sequencing is the event layer and it costs nothing. (4) A crystal-dust emitter on the ring's
circumference, `Snowflake`, drifting up and outward at 1.2 u/s. (5) The opaque layer (L3):
`IceSprites.Debris`, dark blue-grey chips of broken ground thrown low and OUTWARD, on
`Sprite-Unlit-Default`. (6) A `Light2D` at the caster, cold white, radius 3.4, punching to full
in 0.08 s and decaying over 0.5 s.

The frozen targets get `IceSprites.Rime` over their silhouette through `SpriteTintStack` —
never by writing `SpriteRenderer.color` directly, which has exactly one owner.

### `ice_lance` — Ice Lance

**Node:** cryomancy · cost 2 · level 10 · prereq `frost_nova` · role Damage
**Needs:** **S2** (pierce). First user of the piercing mechanic.

A single hard shard that passes THROUGH everything in a line, losing a fifth of its damage per
body. The reward for lining enemies up — a positioning spell wearing a projectile's clothes.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `Projectile` |
| `manaCost` / `cooldownDuration` | 16 / 3.5 |
| `damage` / `speed` / `range` | 30 / 22 / 14 |
| `pierceCount` / `pierceDamageFalloff` | 4 / 0.20 |
| `hitRadius` | 0.5 |
| `element` | `Ice` |
| `particleColor` | `(0.70, 0.92, 1.00)` |
| `statusApplications` | `Slow` 2.0 s, magnitude 0.70, chance 0.60 |

**Look.** Silhouette: a NEEDLE, long on the axis of travel and thin across it — the opposite of
every ball the game already throws, and the reason it reads as piercing before it has pierced
anything. Layers: a stretched `IceSprites.Body` core at roughly 1.1 u by 0.18 u; a brighter
`Rim` inset inside it; a short ghost trail of three fading copies at decreasing alpha, hung on a
NON-SPINNING child (L7 — the shard rolls slowly about its axis and a trail parented to that
would orbit it); and a fine rime emitter shedding backward.

**Each pierce is an EVENT and must look like one.** On every body passed through: a small
`IceWallBurstFX`-style shard spray at the contact point, a 0.04 s white flash on the lance core,
and the core's colour stepped DOWN one notch — so a lance four bodies deep is visibly dimmer
than the one that just left the hand, and the falloff is legible rather than a number in a
tooltip.

### `glacial_step` — Glacial Step

**Node:** cryomancy · cost 2 · level 12 · prereq `frost_nova` · role Mobility
**Needs:** free — `TeleportExecutor` plus a second `Area` application at the origin.

Blink to the cursor. Both the departure point and the arrival point are left frozen: an escape
that punishes whoever was chasing.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `Teleport` |
| `manaCost` / `cooldownDuration` | 18 / 9 |
| `range` | 7 |
| `damage` | 10 |
| `radius` | 1.9 |
| `duration` | 3.0 |
| `element` | `Ice` |
| `particleColor` | `(0.55, 0.85, 1.00)` |
| `spawnAtMouse` | true |
| `statusApplications` | `Slow` 2.5 s, magnitude 0.6, chance 1.0 |

**Look.** Two events, and the ORDER carries the whole spell: the departure fires first and the
arrival lands 0.05 s later, so the eye is dragged from one to the other rather than seeing both
at once. Departure: the caster's silhouette shatters into 20 `IceSprites.Facet` shards thrown
outward and falling, with a rime patch left on the floor. Arrival: the same shards converge
INWARD and resolve into the character, a hard white pop, and a second rime patch.

Both patches are ground-plane sprites under a single squash parent (L7), pinned to 1.9 u by
`Ring` at `radius / 0.39`, holding for 3 s and thawing from the edge inward — a patch that
fades uniformly reads as an alpha ramp, one that shrinks reads as ice melting.

`Vanish` is the flourish family a Teleport inherits, which is exactly right here.

### `frozen_ward` — Frozen Ward

**Node:** cryomancy · cost 2 · level 16 · prereq `ice_lance` · role Protection
**Needs:** **S1** (BuffExecutor).

Armour of ice: defence up sharply, movement down. A deliberate trade rather than a free buff,
and the first spell in the game whose cost is paid in mobility.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `Buff` |
| `manaCost` / `cooldownDuration` | 20 / 14 |
| `duration` | 8 |
| `element` | `Ice` |
| `particleColor` | `(0.60, 0.86, 1.00)` |
| `statModifiers` | `Flat(Defense, +8)` · `Percent(MoveSpeed, -0.20)` · `Percent(MeleeDamage, +0.10)` |
| `buffKey` | `frozen_ward` |

**Look.** Silhouette: a SHELL on the body, following it, never parented to it — parenting
inherits the entity scale and would scale the `Light2D` with it (L5), and
`WeaponSwapFlashFX` already solves the same problem by following. Layers: eight `ShieldSprites.Facet`
plates arranged around the silhouette and sorted by the SIGN of their depth against the caster's
live order, so the character stands INSIDE the armour rather than behind a decal — the one
statement that makes a shell read as a shell, rebased every frame because `YSortEntity` rewrites
the caster's order when they walk. A slow rime creep over the body via `SpriteTintStack`
(`TintLayer` of its own, never a direct colour write), reaching full over the first 0.6 s. A
sparse drift of `Snowflake` motes falling off the shoulders at about one per 0.4 s — the event
layer, deliberately below 30 % duty because a defensive buff should feel steady.

**The last second is a warning.** From `duration - 1.5 s` the facets flicker at a rising rate
and the rime retreats; a buff that simply stops is a buff the player cannot plan around.

### `blizzard` — Blizzard

**Node:** cryomancy · cost 3 · level 22 · prereq `frozen_ward` · role Control
**Needs:** free — `PuddleExecutor` (note it is the last executor still dividing `range` by 16;
fix that while authoring, and see L11).

A standing storm on the ground. Low damage per tick, large radius, long duration, and everything
inside it is slowed hard. Area denial rather than a kill.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `Puddle` |
| `manaCost` / `cooldownDuration` | 26 / 16 |
| `damagePerTick` / `tickPeriod` | 6 / 0.5 |
| `radius` | 4.0 |
| `duration` | 8 |
| `range` | 9 |
| `spawnAtMouse` | true |
| `element` | `Ice` |
| `particleColor` | `(0.72, 0.90, 1.00)` |
| `maxInstances` | 1 |
| `statusApplications` | `Slow` 1.5 s, magnitude 0.45, chance 1.0 · `Freeze` 1.0 s, chance 0.12 |

**Cooldown rule:** 16 against a duration of 8, deliberately. `arcane_flame` and both vortices
recorded the same lesson — with `maxInstances: 1` and a cooldown shorter than the duration the
player always has one out AND can evict their own to reposition it, which is permanent area
denial. `VortexFieldTests` already fails a cooldown below its own field's duration; extend that
test to cover this spell.

**Look.** Silhouette: a COLUMN OF FALLING THINGS with a hard floor boundary, which is a shape
the game has drawn once (the weather system) and never as a spell. Reuse that lesson directly:
a weather effect is a STACK of depth slices, never one system, because a single-system downpour
gives every flake the same size and speed and reads as a decal on the lens. Three slices —
far (small, fast, faint, dense), mid, near (large, slow, sparse, blurred). Falling `Snowflake`
sprites on stretched billboards, and remember the streak texture must be WIDER than it is tall
because the stretched billboard aligns its U axis with velocity.

Under it: the pinned ground ring at `4.0 / 0.39`, breathing in BRIGHTNESS only — a circle that
breathes in SIZE is a promise that moves. A settled-frost splat that accumulates over the first
2 s and thaws over the last 1.5 s. The opaque layer is grey ice grit skittering across the floor
under the wind. A cold `Light2D` at radius 4.2, dimmer than the frost nova's because this one
lives for eight seconds and a bright light held that long flattens everything under it.

The event layer is GUSTS: every 0.9-2.2 s the whole column leans 15-25 degrees for about 0.4 s
and the near slice briefly doubles its rate. Around 28 % duty.

## Verdant Rites — 3 nodes to 8

*"Ask the ground for help. It usually agrees."* Accent `(0.45, 0.85, 0.40)`.
Affinities: elven, dwarf. The school owns poison, root and the game's only living allies.

### `thorn_burst` — Thorn Burst

**Node:** verdant · cost 1 · level 5 · prereq `laser_beam_green` · role Damage
**Needs:** free (`AreaExecutor`).

Thorns erupt from the ground around the caster. Modest hit, reliable poison.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `Area` |
| `manaCost` / `cooldownDuration` | 12 / 5 |
| `damage` | 16 |
| `radius` | 2.8 |
| `element` | `Nature` |
| `particleColor` | `(0.50, 0.88, 0.42)` |
| `castAnchor` | `Feet` |
| `statusApplications` | `Poison` 5.0 s, magnitude 4, chance 0.85 |

**Look.** Silhouette: SPIKES from below, so the whole effect must have a clear "before" —
the ground cracks first. Sequence over 0.35 s: `RootSprites.Crack` decals fan out across the
floor (0.10 s), then 16-20 `RootSprites.Tendril` thorns punch upward in a ragged ring, each with
a small `Burst` at its base. The thorns are the SILHOUETTE and they are NOT additive: this is
matter, not light, so the tendrils are `Sprite-Unlit-Default` in deep green with a lighter tip,
and only the burst at each base is additive. That inversion is what makes it read as the world
being disturbed rather than as a spell being drawn over it (L3, applied to the main layer
instead of a debris layer).

Then they retract over 0.5 s, leaving `RootSprites.Clod` soil chips that fall and stay for a
second. A short green `Light2D` flash at the crack moment, radius 2.6, decaying fast — plants
do not glow, so the light is an accent on the eruption and not an ambience.

### `entangle` — Entangle

**Node:** verdant · cost 2 · level 9 · prereq `thorn_burst` · role Control
**Needs:** free (`AreaExecutor` + the `Root` status, which is fully implemented).

Roots seize everything in a patch. No damage at all: the feet are refused, the hands are not.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `Area` |
| `manaCost` / `cooldownDuration` | 16 / 10 |
| `damage` | 0 |
| `radius` | 2.6 |
| `range` | 8 |
| `spawnAtMouse` | true |
| `element` | `Nature` |
| `particleColor` | `(0.42, 0.80, 0.36)` |
| `statusApplications` | `Root` 3.0 s, chance 1.0 |

**Look.** `RootWhipFX` already exists and already solves the hard half — it grows roots out of
the ground and holds the feet it catches. Reuse it: per rooted target, three to four stems
climbing the ankles and closing, plus a ground ring pinned at `2.6 / 0.39` marking the patch.

The one thing to add is **release**: when the root expires the stems must WITHER — brown, slack,
and falling away over 0.3 s — because a root that vanishes cleanly gives the player no frame in
which to notice they can move again. `ISpellEffectDissipates` is the seam; without it an
eviction or a zone change skips the wither entirely.

Zero damage is the design. A control spell that also does damage is a damage spell.

### `barkskin` — Barkskin

**Node:** verdant · cost 2 · level 13 · prereq `entangle` · role Protection
**Needs:** **S1** (BuffExecutor).

Bark over the skin: health and defence, no downside, moderate duration. The school's answer to
attrition.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `Buff` |
| `manaCost` / `cooldownDuration` | 18 / 18 |
| `duration` | 12 |
| `element` | `Nature` |
| `particleColor` | `(0.55, 0.78, 0.35)` |
| `statModifiers` | `Flat(MaxHp, +40)` · `Flat(Defense, +5)` · `Percent(ManaRegen, +0.15)` |
| `buffKey` | `barkskin` |

**Look.** Bark GROWS. Over the first 0.8 s, `RootSprites.Tendril` strips creep up the body from
the feet — six to eight of them, opaque, brown-green, sorted against the caster's live order so
the front strips draw over the body and the back ones behind it. That split is the same
statement `ShieldSphereFX` makes and it is what stops the effect being a decal.

The body itself darkens and desaturates slightly through a `SpriteTintStack` layer (multiply,
so it reads as bark rather than as tint). A slow drift of leaf motes off the shoulders, one
every 0.6 s, additive and faint — the only additive layer in the whole rig, which is what makes
it read as living wood rather than as a magic shell. No light: bark does not glow.

**`Flat(MaxHp, +40)` needs care.** The push must be idempotent — `Health.SetMaxHp`, not
`IncreaseMaxHp` — or the recompute that runs when an unrelated buff expires grants the bonus
again and heals the player a little each time. `PlayerStats` already enforces this; the note is
here because a buff granting max HP is the exact case that breaks it.

### `spore_cloud` — Spore Cloud

**Node:** verdant · cost 2 · level 16 · prereq `entangle` · role Control
**Needs:** free (`SmokeEmitterExecutor`).

A lingering cloud that poisons and blinds. Denies a corridor without holding a wall.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `SmokeEmitter` |
| `manaCost` / `cooldownDuration` | 20 / 12 |
| `damagePerTick` / `tickPeriod` | 4 / 0.6 |
| `radius` | 3.0 |
| `duration` | 7 |
| `range` | 8 |
| `spawnAtMouse` | true |
| `element` | `Nature` |
| `particleColor` | `(0.62, 0.80, 0.38)` |
| `maxInstances` | 2 |
| `statusApplications` | `Poison` 4.0 s, magnitude 5, chance 0.9 · `Slow` 1.2 s, magnitude 0.8, chance 0.5 |

**Look.** Silhouette: a VOLUME, and volumes are the hardest thing to draw in a 2D top-down
game because there is no depth cue. The answer is the same as the blizzard's: depth slices. Two
of them plus a floor layer. The near slice is large, slow, sparse and pale; the far slice is
small, faster and denser. Both drift with the shared `WeatherWind` gust field, which already
exists and is ticked once per frame so every reader samples the same gust — a cloud that ignores
the wind while rain slants past it is the sort of inconsistency that reads as cheapness.

The floor layer is a sickly green haze at low alpha, pinned to 3.0 u. The opaque layer is spore
grit settling out of the cloud onto the ground and staying there until the cloud lifts.

Event layer: every 1.2-2.5 s a puff BLOOMS somewhere in the volume — a quick local expansion and
fade, about 25 % duty. Without it a cloud is a texture within a second (L4).

Light: a very dim green `Light2D` at 3.2, which is doing one job only — making the cloud's own
particles pick up colour at night so it does not read at noon brightness in a dark room (L14 is
about not gating the light; this is the neighbouring point, that a coloured volume needs a light
to sit in the world at all).

### `summon_wolf` — Summon Wolf

**Node:** verdant · cost 3 · level 20 · prereq `barkskin` · role Summon
**Needs:** **S8** (allied summon). Not authorable before that lands.

One ally that chases and bites. Times out.

**Look.** The arrival is the spell — after that the wolf is an entity with its own animation and
the VFX budget belongs to its lifetime, not its entrance. Sequence: a ground sigil expands
(`Conjure` is the flourish family a Summon already inherits, which is correct), roots part, and
the wolf rises THROUGH the floor over 0.4 s with a soil burst and `RootSprites.Clod` chips
thrown outward. Hold a faint green rim on the creature for its whole life, sorted with it, so
the player can always tell a summon from a monster at a glance — a summon indistinguishable from
an enemy is a UI failure wearing a VFX costume.

The last 2 s of `summonDuration` fade that rim to nothing and add drifting leaf motes, then the
body sinks back into the ground rather than blinking out.

## Umbramancy — 4 nodes to 8

*"Not being seen is a form of armour."* Accent `(0.45, 0.35, 0.55)`.
Affinities: elven, mague. Displacement, debuff and the game's one genuinely strange spell.

### `shadow_step` — Shadow Step

**Node:** shadow · cost 2 · level 10 · prereq `smoke` · role Mobility
**Needs:** free for the blink; the brief untargetable window is a small addition to
`StatusEffectManager` or a flag on `Health`.

Blink through shadow to the cursor and arrive behind the world for a heartbeat. Half a second
of being unhittable, and a slower cooldown than `teleport` to pay for it.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `Teleport` |
| `manaCost` / `cooldownDuration` | 16 / 8 |
| `range` | 8 |
| `duration` | 0.5 |
| `element` | `Dark` |
| `particleColor` | `(0.55, 0.40, 0.72)` |
| `spawnAtMouse` | true |

**Look.** Silhouette: the character's OWN outline, twice. Departure leaves a standing violet
after-image of the exact pose, which then peels apart into vertical ribbons and is drawn
downward into the floor over 0.25 s. Arrival is the same ribbons rising and knitting shut. Both
are additive and deliberately DARK-coloured rather than low-alpha (L2) — a deep violet at high
alpha covers the silhouette and adds dark light, which is what shadow should do; a faint pale
version reads as a ghost, which is a different spell.

Between them, a thin line of motes marks the path travelled, arriving in order from origin to
destination, so the direction is legible even when the two ends are off different edges of the
eye's attention.

The untargetable window is `SpriteTintStack` at 55 % alpha with a slow violet shimmer — and it
must END with a visible snap back to full opacity, because a window the player cannot see
closing is a window they cannot use.

### `void_lance` — Void Lance

**Node:** shadow · cost 2 · level 14 · prereq `laser_beam_black` · role Damage
**Needs:** **S2** (pierce). Second user, which is the point of building it as a flag.

The shadow counterpart to `ice_lance`: fewer bodies, no falloff at all, and it leaves poison in
the wound.

| Field | Value |

| `manaCost` / `cooldownDuration` | 18 / 4 |
| `damage` / `speed` / `range` | 26 / 19 / 13 |

alike waste the mechanic. Where the shard is a bright needle with a trail behind it, the void

shape of something the world is healing over. Layers: an opaque near-black core (the L3 layer,
and here it is the main body); a thin violet additive rim slightly larger than it; a wake of
four to six motes that spread outward from the flight line and are pulled back in.

Each pierce blooms a small dark burst that momentarily DIMS the additive rim before it recovers
— the reverse of the ice lance's white flash, and legible for the same reason.

### `curse_of_frailty` — Curse of Frailty

**Node:** shadow · cost 3 · level 18 · prereq `void_lance` · role Control
**Needs:** **S7** (enemy debuff, built as a `VulnerableEffect` status).

A single target takes more damage from every source for a while. The party spell in a game with
no party — it makes the player's own burst window.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `Projectile` |
| `manaCost` / `cooldownDuration` | 20 / 12 |
| `damage` / `speed` / `range` | 5 / 24 / 12 |
| `duration` | 8 |
| `element` | `Dark` |
| `particleColor` | `(0.62, 0.32, 0.60)` |
| `statusApplications` | `Vulnerable` 8.0 s, magnitude 0.30, chance 1.0 |

`Vulnerable` is a NEW `StatusEffectKind`. **Append it, never insert** — `EntityStats.statusImmunities`
and `SpellDefinition.statusApplications` both serialise the enum as its integer, so renumbering
repoints every authored immunity and every authored application at the wrong effect without
touching a file.

**Look.** The projectile is almost nothing on purpose — a slow violet wisp, small, low speed —
because the spell's whole visual budget belongs to the MARK it leaves.

The mark is a sigil that hangs over the target and follows them: a slowly counter-rotating pair
of rings (one clockwise, one not, which is what stops a rotating ring reading as a texture),
drawn on `ElementalSprites.Ring` in dark violet, plus three motes orbiting on a squashed
ground-plane ellipse at the target's feet so the effect exists in the world and not only above
it. The target's own sprite takes a violet `SpriteTintStack` layer at low strength.

Event layer: every 1.4-2.6 s the sigil PULSES — rings snap outward and back over 0.2 s, motes
brighten. Roughly 15 % duty; a curse should feel patient.

Every hit landed on a cursed target adds a violet flash to the normal hit feedback, which is how
the player learns the curse is doing something without reading a number.

### `raise_thrall` — Raise Thrall

**Node:** shadow · cost 3 · level 24 · prereq `curse_of_frailty` · role Summon
**Needs:** **S8** (allied summon) plus the mark. The most interesting spell in the 27 and the
last to be built.

**Cast it on a LIVING enemy.** Nothing happens immediately. The target is marked; if it dies
while the mark holds, it rises as an ally under the player's control for a while, then collapses
for good.

This is a better design than raising a corpse and it is cheaper to build, which is unusual
enough to be worth stating plainly:

- **The hook lands while the entity still exists.** A corpse spell has to hook `Health.OnDeath`
  or `DeathSequenceController`, then find a body that `deathDisappearTime` may already have
  despawned, and reconstruct which `MonsterDefinition` it was from something that is no longer
  there. The mark is carried BY the target, so at the moment of death every fact needed —
  definition, level, position, facing — is still on a live GameObject.
- **It is a real decision.** The player spends mana and a cast on a bet placed BEFORE the kill,
  on a target they think they can finish inside the window. Spending it on something that then
  walks away is the cost, and a spell that can be wasted is a spell worth aiming.
- **It telegraphs to the enemy side too.** A marked monster is visibly marked, which makes the
  ten seconds before it dies tense rather than administrative.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `Projectile` |
| `manaCost` / `cooldownDuration` | 30 / 28 |
| `damage` / `speed` / `range` | 0 / 20 / 11 |
| `duration` | 10 (the mark's window) |
| `summonDuration` | 18 (how long the thrall serves) |
| `maxInstances` | 1 |
| `element` | `Dark` |
| `particleColor` | `(0.60, 0.35, 0.75)` |
| `statusApplications` | `Marked` 10.0 s, chance 1.0 |

**The mechanic, precisely.**

1. The bolt applies a `ThrallMarkEffect` (a `StatusEffect`, so it inherits duration, refresh,
   immunity and cleanup for free — the same argument as S7).
2. If the target dies while marked, the effect's death hook spawns an ally from that target's
   own `MonsterDefinition` at that position, with `summonDuration` seconds to live.
3. If the mark expires first, it fades and the cast is spent. No refund. That is the bet.
4. `maxInstances: 1` — one thrall at a time. Raising a second releases the first, and the
   release must be visible or the player will think the spell failed.

Three rules the implementation must not get wrong. **The thrall's HP is the monster's own, not
the player's** — raising a boss must not hand the player a boss. Scale it down explicitly, and
gate the whole spell against anything carrying `BossPhaseController`. **The thrall keeps the
dead monster's appearance**, tinted, because "that thing I just killed is now fighting for me"
is the entire fantasy and a generic minion throws it away. And **the mark must survive the
target being frozen, stunned, rooted or hit by anything else**, which it does automatically by
being a status effect rather than a bespoke component — `StatusEffectManager.Apply` replaces
only an effect of the SAME type.

**Look — the mark.** A closed sigil over the target: an outer ring turning slowly, an inner
glyph turning the other way, three violet motes orbiting the feet on a ground-plane ellipse.
Where `curse_of_frailty` pulses patiently, this one **tightens as the target weakens** — the
rings contract, the rate climbs, the colour heats from violet toward a pale magenta as the
target's HP fraction falls. At below 25 % HP the sigil is visibly urgent. That single coupling
is what turns the mark from decoration into information, and it is the piece to build first.

At `duration - 2 s` the sigil begins to unravel: the outer ring breaks into arcs that drift
apart. An expiring mark and a firing mark must be unmistakable at a glance.

**Look — the rising.** The biggest single moment in the 27, and it earns the budget because it
is rare. Six beats over about 1.1 s:

1. **0.00 s** — the kill lands, the mark FLARES white-violet and collapses inward to a point at
   the corpse's chest. Everything else on screen is quiet for 0.15 s. That silence is the beat
   the whole effect hangs on, and cutting it is the one change that would ruin this.
2. **0.15 s** — the ground under the body cracks (`RootSprites.Crack`, retinted violet) and a
   dark ground ring opens, pinned by `Ring` at the thrall's own body radius.
3. **0.30 s** — violet motes stream UP out of the floor and INTO the body, which is the exact
   reverse of the death effect the player just watched. Around 40 of them, converging.
4. **0.55 s** — the body rises. `GrayscaleDeath`'s desaturation runs BACKWARDS — colour
   returning to a corpse, driven through `SpriteTintStack` and not by writing the renderer.
5. **0.85 s** — a hard violet rim ignites around the silhouette and holds for the thrall's whole
   life, marking it as the player's. Sorted against the creature's own live order, rebased every
   frame (L6).
6. **1.10 s** — control passes to the FSM brain. A short shockwave ring on the floor and a
   violet `Light2D` punch at radius 3.0 decaying over 0.6 s.

Audio: nothing at all for the first 0.15 s, then a low sub-bass swell, then a dry crack at the
rise. The silence is the composition.

**Look — the collapse.** At the end of `summonDuration` the rim dims, the body desaturates
forward this time, and it falls into a violet mote burst that drifts up and out. The player must
be able to tell a thrall that TIMED OUT from one that was KILLED: killed collapses instantly
with a hard shatter, timed-out sinks slowly. Same information rule as the two ends of the mark.

## Radiance — 5 nodes to 9

*"Keeping people alive is the harder half of any fight."* Accent `(1.00, 0.95, 0.72)`.
Affinities: valkyrie, mague. The school with two nodes today that actually heal.

### `radiant_burst` — Radiant Burst

**Node:** radiance · cost 1 · level 6 · prereq `lightball` · role Damage
**Needs:** free (`AreaExecutor`), plus a self-heal on cast which `healPerTick` already models.

Light detonates at the caster. Damages everything around and heals the caster for a share of it.
The school's only offensive spell and its most reliable panic button.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `Area` |
| `manaCost` / `cooldownDuration` | 15 / 7 |
| `damage` | 22 |
| `radius` | 3.0 |
| `healPerTick` | 18 |
| `element` | `Light` |
| `particleColor` | `(1.00, 0.93, 0.68)` |
| `castAnchor` | `Center` |

**Look.** Silhouette: a SPHERE of light that expands and is gone — the only spell in the 27 that
is allowed to be purely additive, because light is the one thing that genuinely is. Layers, all
on the shared additive material: a `HotCore` that punches to overdriven colour
(around 2.6 on the RGB, alpha left alone — L2) and shrinks; a `Glow` and a `Halo` that expand
past it; the ground ring pinned at `3.0 / 0.39` sweeping outward; and gold `Sparkle` motes
thrown outward and rising.

The whole thing is over in 0.45 s. **A heal that lingers reads as an aura**, and this is a
detonation.

Two beats separate it from every other burst in the game. The caster is briefly WHITE-tinted
through `SpriteTintStack` — the heal is on them, so the light must be too. And there is a
half-frame of DARKNESS first: the screen grade dips for 0.05 s before the flash, which is what
makes the flash read as bright on a screen that is already bright at noon. Contrast, not
absolute value.

`Light2D` at radius 3.4, gold, full in 0.05 s, out in 0.35 s.

### `blessing` — Blessing

**Node:** radiance · cost 2 · level 11 · prereq `radiant_burst` · role Healing
**Needs:** **S1** (BuffExecutor).

Spell power and regeneration for a long window. The buff a caster opens a fight with.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `Buff` |
| `manaCost` / `cooldownDuration` | 18 / 20 |
| `duration` | 15 |
| `element` | `Light` |
| `particleColor` | `(1.00, 0.95, 0.75)` |
| `statModifiers` | `Percent(SpellPower, +0.18)` · `Flat(ManaRegen, +2)` · `Percent(XpGain, +0.05)` |
| `buffKey` | `blessing` |

**Look.** Silhouette: a COLUMN of light from above, then a held halo. The cast is a shaft
descending onto the caster over 0.5 s — narrow at the top, wide at the floor, which is the
opposite taper to a vortex and reads as something arriving rather than something being taken.
Reuse `FlameConeFX`'s lesson: slices along the axis whose cross extent is the shape's real width
at that height, never a `LineRenderer`.

The sustained half is deliberately quiet: a thin gold ring orbiting at chest height, tilted onto
the ground plane by a single squash parent (L7), and a `Sparkle` mote lifting off the shoulders
about every 0.7 s. Around 12 % duty. A 15-second buff that is busy is a 15-second distraction.

Last 2 s: the ring's rate climbs and its radius contracts, the standard expiry warning.

### `sanctuary` — Sanctuary

**Node:** radiance · cost 3 · level 17 · prereq `blessing` · role Healing
**Needs:** **S4** (area totem).

A standing totem that heals everything friendly inside its circle. The first spell in the game
that heals an area rather than a person.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `Totem` |
| `manaCost` / `cooldownDuration` | 24 / 22 |
| `healPerTick` / `tickPeriod` | 10 / 1.0 |
| `radius` | 3.4 |
| `duration` | 10 |
| `range` | 6 |
| `spawnAtMouse` | true |
| `maxInstances` | 1 |
| `totemKind` | `heal` |
| `element` | `Light` |
| `particleColor` | `(1.00, 0.94, 0.70)` |

**Look.** Silhouette: a PILLAR with a floor. The totem itself is an opaque object (L3 — this is
the layer that says something was placed in the world), a pale stone shaft about 1.4 u tall with
a gold band. Around it: the pinned ground ring at `3.4 / 0.39`, a low dome of light over the
circle at very low alpha, and gold motes rising from the floor inside the ring and dissolving at
head height.

The event layer is the TICK, and it must be one: on every heal pulse the ring brightens sharply
and a wave of motes lifts together. One second apart, roughly 20 % duty — and because it is
synchronised to the actual heal, the player can count the ticks, which is a rare case of a VFX
beat carrying literal mechanical information.

Per healed entity, a small gold ripple over the silhouette. Never a colour write on the
renderer — a `SpriteTintStack` layer, which is the rule that has eight prior violations behind
it.

`Light2D` at 3.6, gold, steady, brightening on each tick.

### `guardian_light` — Guardian Light

**Node:** radiance · cost 3 · level 21 · prereq `sanctuary` · role Protection
**Needs:** **S6** (absorb shield).

A shell that absorbs a fixed amount of damage and then breaks. Unlike `sphere_magic_shield`, it
is not invincibility — it is a number that visibly runs out.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `SphereMagicShield` |
| `manaCost` / `cooldownDuration` | 22 / 24 |
| `duration` | 10 |
| `wallHP` | 120 (reused as the absorb pool) |
| `radius` | 1.1 |
| `element` | `Light` |
| `particleColor` | `(1.00, 0.96, 0.80)` |

**Look.** Start from `ShieldSphereFX`, which already gets the hard part right: facets and motes
sorted by the SIGN of their depth against the caster's live order, so the character is INSIDE
the sphere. Keep all of it, and add the one thing an absorb shield needs and an invincibility
shield does not — **the pool must be visible.**

Three coupled readings, all driven off the remaining fraction: facet OPACITY falls as the pool
drains; hairline CRACKS accumulate across the shell (`IceSprites.Crack`, retinted gold), a new
one at each quarter lost; and the colour cools from warm gold toward pale white as it empties.
Together those make "one more hit" legible without a bar.

Each absorbed blow drives a ripple placed by GEODESIC distance across the shell, so it wraps
around the far side and converges at the antipode — straight-line screen distance draws a disc
that stops at the silhouette, which is a ripple on a plate rather than on a ball. `Health.OnDamageBlocked`
already fires only for a blow genuinely turned away, which is the correct hook.

The BREAK is the payoff: the shell shatters outward into facets that fade, with a hard white
flash and a short shockwave ring. Timing out instead is a quiet dissolve. Same information rule
as the thrall's two endings.

## Stormcalling — 4 nodes to 7

*"The sky keeps no ledger and settles all at once."* Accent `(0.95, 0.90, 0.35)`.
Affinities: mague, valkyrie.

### `seeking_shard` — Seeking Shard

**Node:** storm · cost 2 · level 9 · prereq `lightning` · role Damage
**Needs:** **S2** (homing).

A spark that hunts. Slower than any other projectile in the game, and it does not miss.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `Projectile` |
| `manaCost` / `cooldownDuration` | 14 / 3 |
| `damage` / `speed` / `range` | 22 / 11 / 16 |
| `homingStrength` / `homingRange` | 220 deg/s / 6 |
| `hitRadius` | 0.4 |
| `element` | `Lightning` |
| `particleColor` | `(1.00, 0.95, 0.45)` |
| `statusApplications` | `Stun` 0.5 s, chance 0.20 |

**Look.** The whole spell is its PATH, so the trail is not decoration here — it is the thing
being drawn. A bright `Bolt` core with a long ribbon behind it that records the actual curve
flown, hung on a non-spinning child so it follows rather than orbits (L7, the mistake
`ElementalProjectileVisual` shipped).

The turn must be VISIBLE: the core banks, the ribbon widens on the outside of the arc, and small
sparks shed tangentially — thrown off the curve, which is what makes a turn read as a turn
rather than as a repositioning.

Acquisition is an event and deserves a frame: when the shard locks on, it FLASHES once and the
target takes a brief yellow rim. That single beat is the difference between "it happens to be
following me" and "it is hunting me".

### `thunderclap` — Thunderclap

**Node:** storm · cost 2 · level 14 · prereq `seeking_shard` · role Control
**Needs:** free (`AreaExecutor` + the `Stun` status).

A flat crack of sound and light around the caster. Small damage, reliable short stun.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `Area` |
| `manaCost` / `cooldownDuration` | 18 / 11 |
| `damage` | 20 |
| `radius` | 3.6 |
| `element` | `Lightning` |
| `particleColor` | `(1.00, 0.97, 0.60)` |
| `castAnchor` | `Center` |
| `statusApplications` | `Stun` 1.4 s, chance 0.85 |

**Look.** Silhouette: a SHOCKWAVE, which is a ring with an inside — the air between the caster
and the ring must distort, or it is just another expanding circle. Layers: a near-white core
flash at the caster lasting three frames; a hard ring sweeping to 3.6 u in 0.12 s (fast, because
sound is fast, and the speed IS the character of this spell); six to eight `Bolt` forks along the
ring, each appearing as the ring reaches its angle; a dust wave on the ground under it; and the
opaque layer, grit and small stones jumping straight up and falling.

**Use the global light, not a local one.** A clap is an event in the room, and `SkyFlash` already
composes into `DayNightCycle.UpdateLighting` for exactly this — a brief global lift plus the local
`Light2D`. That is what separates a clap from a flare.

Stunned targets get the existing stun feedback; do not invent a second one.

### `static_field` — Static Field

**Node:** storm · cost 3 · level 19 · prereq `thunderclap` · role Damage
**Needs:** **S5** (damaging aura).

A field around the caster that shocks whatever stays near them. Sustained rather than burst, and
the only spell in the school that rewards standing still.

**Look.** Silhouette: a DOME the caster carries. Follows rather than parents (L5). A faint
spherical shell at low alpha, sorted front and back against the caster's live order the way the
shield is, plus the pinned ground ring at `2.6 / 0.39` so the reach is honest.

The event layer is the whole spell: **arcs that crawl the shell**, appearing between two points
on the dome and gone in 0.1 s, at 0.25-0.7 s intervals. Roughly 25 % duty. And every arc that
fires while an enemy is inside should preferentially terminate ON that enemy, which turns a
decorative layer into a damage indicator at no extra cost.

The `Light2D` flickers with the arcs rather than sitting steady — a field held for eight seconds
at constant brightness is L4's failure exactly.

## Martial Forms — 5 nodes to 8

*"No words. Just the weight of the thing in your hands."* Accent `(0.82, 0.80, 0.74)`.
Affinities: dwarf, barbarian, valkyrie. The school with no magic, which is a constraint worth
protecting: nothing here glows because it is enchanted.

### `scatter_volley` — Scatter Volley

**Node:** martial · cost 2 · level 10 · prereq `dash` · role Damage
**Needs:** **S2** (volley).

Five blades thrown in a fan. Each is weak; the cone is not. The first spell in the game whose
damage depends on how close the target is.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `Projectile` |
| `manaCost` / `cooldownDuration` | 12 / 5 |
| `damage` / `speed` / `range` | 11 / 20 / 9 |
| `projectileCount` / `spreadDegrees` | 5 / 46 |
| `hitRadius` | 0.35 |
| `element` | (leave empty — this is steel) |
| `particleColor` | `(0.86, 0.86, 0.82)` |
| `usesAttackAnimation` | true |

**Look.** Silhouette: five hard, small, SPINNING objects — and they must not be five copies of
one another. Give each blade its own spin rate and a small random size jitter, because a
perfectly uniform fan reads as a UI element rather than as thrown steel.

`ElementalSprites.Blade`, opaque, on `Sprite-Unlit-Default` — **there is no additive layer in
this spell at all**, and that is the design. Every other entry in the 27 is light; this one is
metal, and the contrast is what gives Martial Forms an identity next to eight schools of magic.
The only bright element is a thin specular glint that flashes as each blade's spin brings its
edge past the camera, roughly twice per second per blade — which is the event layer, and it is
free.

Each blade drags a very short motion smear (two ghost copies at low alpha, non-spinning child).
Impact is a spark burst and a shallow chip decal on whatever it hit.

The cast throws with the ATTACK animation, so the flourish family is `Edge`: sparks off the
swing arc, no circle drawn. Correct — a thrown blade summons nothing.

### `war_cry` — War Cry

**Node:** martial · cost 2 · level 15 · prereq `scatter_volley` · role Protection
**Needs:** **S1** (BuffExecutor).

Melee damage and movement up for a while. No projectile, no target, no subtlety.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `Buff` |
| `manaCost` / `cooldownDuration` | 14 / 20 |
| `duration` | 10 |
| `particleColor` | `(0.95, 0.72, 0.45)` |
| `statModifiers` | `Percent(MeleeDamage, +0.25)` · `Percent(MoveSpeed, +0.12)` · `Percent(MeleeCooldown, -0.10)` |
| `buffKey` | `war_cry` |

**Look.** The problem to solve: this is a self-buff on a character forty pixels tall, which is
the exact case `SpellCastFlourishFX` was written for — "a cast pose is not a cast", because the
difference between an idle frame and a shout is a few pixels and everything readable has to
happen in LIGHT around the body.

Silhouette: a RING travelling outward at ground level, plus heat on the body. The cast is a hard
outward shockwave ring on the floor reaching 4 u in 0.2 s — it does nothing mechanically and it
is the whole reason the shout reads as a shout. Dust lifts along it. The camera takes a short
kick, and the character's own sprite flashes warm through `SpriteTintStack`.

The sustained half is minimal and warm: a faint orange rim on the silhouette and occasional heat
motes rising, about one every 0.8 s. **No orbiting ring, no sigil** — those belong to the magic
schools and using them here would erase the distinction Martial Forms is built on.

Expiry: the rim cools to nothing over the last 1.5 s.

### `leap_slam` — Leap Slam

**Node:** martial · cost 3 · level 20 · prereq `war_cry` · role Mobility
**Needs:** free-ish — a `Dash` to the cursor composed with an `Area` on landing. The composition
is small new code, but both halves already exist.

Leap to a point and land hard. Movement and damage in one button, which is the pattern every
melee class in every game is built around and this one does not have yet.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `Dash` |
| `manaCost` / `cooldownDuration` | 20 / 12 |
| `distance` / `range` | 6 / 6 |
| `collisionDamage` | 0 |
| `damage` | 30 |
| `radius` | 2.6 |
| `knockback` | 6 |
| `spawnAtMouse` | true |
| `particleColor` | `(0.90, 0.80, 0.62)` |
| `usesAttackAnimation` | true |
| `statusApplications` | `Stun` 0.8 s, chance 0.5 |

**Look.** Three beats and the middle one is the hard part. **Launch**: a dust ring at the feet
and a downward compression on the sprite for two frames. **Flight**: the character is airborne
in a top-down game, which the projection cannot show — so the cues are a SHADOW that separates
from the feet and shrinks, and a slight upward sprite offset along an arc. Those two together are
the entire illusion of height, and dropping the shadow loses it completely. **Landing**: this is
where the budget goes — a hard ground ring pinned at `2.6 / 0.39`, radial dust, `RootSprites.Clod`
chips thrown outward and up (the opaque layer), a crack decal that stays for a couple of seconds,
a sharp camera kick DOWNWARD, and hit-stop of about 0.06 s.

**No zoom punch, ever.** `CameraPixelSnap` derives its lattice from the live ortho size and a
punch of a few percent lands between rungs and makes every tile on screen crawl. There is no
seam-legal zoom punch in a 16-PPU game. Weight is expressed through kick, shake frequency, trauma
decay, hit-stop and lead freeze.

## Pyromancy — 6 nodes to 8

*"Fire is the only school that answers before it is finished being asked."* Accent
`(1.00, 0.45, 0.15)`. Affinities: mague, barbarian.

### `charged_bolt` — Charged Bolt

**Node:** pyromancy · cost 2 · level 8 · prereq `laser_beam_red` · role Damage
**Needs:** **S3** (charged cast). The flagship of the four new mechanics.

Hold to grow it, release to throw it. At minimum charge it is a weaker fireball; at full charge
it is the hardest single hit in the school.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `Projectile` |
| `manaCost` / `cooldownDuration` | 12 / 4 |
| `damage` / `speed` / `range` | 24 / 15 / 15 |
| `chargeMaxSeconds` | 1.6 |
| `chargeMinFraction` | 0.45 |
| `chargeDamageMultiplier` | 2.6 |
| `chargeScaleMultiplier` | 2.0 |
| `hitRadius` | 0.55 (scales with charge) |
| `radius` | 1.8 (impact splash at full charge) |
| `element` | `Fire` |
| `particleColor` | `(1.00, 0.48, 0.14)` |
| `statusApplications` | `Burn` 4.0 s, magnitude 6, chance 0.75 |

**Look — and the charge is the spell.** The projectile matters less than the 1.6 seconds before
it exists, because that is the only window in this game where the player is holding power in
their hand and can see it.

The charge builds in the caster's palm and it grows in DENSITY and BEHAVIOUR, not merely in size
(L12). Across the ramp: the core goes from a dim ember to overdriven white-orange (colour, not
alpha — L2); orbiting motes go from three to fourteen and their orbit tightens and speeds up;
ground light spreads from nothing to a 2 u pool under the caster; heat shimmer appears past 60 %;
and above 80 % the ball starts shedding sparks that fall and die on the floor — the opaque layer
(L3), and the one that says the world is being affected.

**Three beats make the charge readable**, and they are worth more than any amount of particle
count. At 100 % the whole rig SNAPS once — a hard flash and a momentary contraction — which is
how the player learns where full is without a bar. Between 45 % and 100 % the pitch of a rising
synth tone tracks the charge exactly. And the caster's sprite brightens through `SpriteTintStack`
on the same curve.

Release throws it with a recoil kick proportional to charge. Impact at full charge splashes; at
minimum charge it does not, and that difference must be visible.

Holding past `chargeMaxSeconds` does nothing extra and must LOOK like it does nothing extra —
the rig settles into a steady loop, so the player is told to let go.

### `cinder_trail` — Cinder Trail

**Node:** pyromancy · cost 3 · level 18 · prereq `charged_bolt` · role Control
**Needs:** small new controller. The emitter follows the caster and drops timed `Puddle`-like
patches; both halves exist, the composition does not.

For a while, everywhere the caster walks burns behind them. A kiting spell — the only one in the
game that rewards moving rather than standing.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `Puddle` |
| `manaCost` / `cooldownDuration` | 22 / 16 |
| `damagePerTick` / `tickPeriod` | 7 / 0.5 |
| `radius` | 1.2 (per patch) |
| `duration` | 8 (how long the caster burns the ground) |
| `ttl` | 3.5 (how long each patch lasts) |
| `followCaster` | true |
| `element` | `Fire` |
| `particleColor` | `(1.00, 0.42, 0.10)` |
| `maxInstances` | 1 |
| `statusApplications` | `Burn` 3.0 s, magnitude 5, chance 0.8 |

**Look.** Silhouette: a PATH, which no spell in the game currently draws. A patch is dropped
every 0.35 s of movement (never on a stationary caster, or standing still would pile eight
patches on one tile), and each patch is a small independent fire: a scorch decal underneath that
is opaque and dark, low flame tongues on `KiSprites.Tongue`, a few embers rising, and a small
`Light2D`.

Two things make the trail read as one continuous thing rather than as beads. Consecutive patches
OVERLAP by roughly a third of their radius. And each patch's ignition is staggered by its
distance from the caster, so the fire visibly chases the player's footsteps rather than appearing
all at once.

Each patch dies from the EDGE inward, leaving its scorch decal behind for a couple of seconds
after the flame is gone. That residue is what makes the trail feel like it happened to the world.

## Arcana — 8 nodes to 9

*"The school that studies the other schools."* Accent `(0.70, 0.45, 1.00)`.
Affinities: mague, elven. It is already the deepest school, so it takes exactly one node — the
one thing it lacks.

### `arcane_barrier` — Arcane Barrier

**Node:** arcane · cost 2 · level 16 · prereq `mine_basic` · role Protection
**Needs:** free — `WallExecutor` with `blockProjectiles: true` and `blockUnits: false`, both of
which are existing authored fields.

A wall that stops projectiles and lets bodies through. The inverse of `wall_ice`, and a genuinely
different tool: cover against casters, useless against a melee rush.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `type` | `Wall` |
| `manaCost` / `cooldownDuration` | 16 / 10 |
| `wallWidth` / `wallHeight` | 4.5 / 0.35 (**world units** — see L11) |
| `wallHP` | 80 |
| `blockProjectiles` / `blockUnits` | true / false |
| `duration` | 7 |
| `range` | 5 |
| `spawnAtMouse` | true |
| `element` | `Arcane` |
| `particleColor` | `(0.72, 0.48, 1.00)` |
| `maxInstances` | 1 |

**`wallWidth`/`wallHeight` are the first Python-pixel sighting in this project's history.** The
shipped `wall_ice` authored 12.5 x 3.125 against an executor dividing by 32, and resolved to a
barrier **0.78 u wide and 0.049 u tall** — twelve screen pixels by less than one. Author these in
world units and verify on screen before calling it done.

**Look.** Silhouette: a LINE, standing up. Start from `IceWallVisual`, which is the project's
answer to exactly this shape and exists because `AreaFXRig` could not draw it: an UNROTATED,
UNSCALED root, elements placed along the axis by POSITION so they stand up on screen whichever
way the wall runs, absolute per-child sizes, a Box emitter as long as the wall, and lights spread
along it. Only the collider child is rotated.

Retint to arcane violet and change one thing: this barrier is **translucent, because it must not
hide what is behind it.** A wall the player cannot see through is a wall they will not stand
behind. Layers: a low-alpha violet pane; a hard bright edge along the top; a hexagonal lattice
that is normally faint.

The event layer is IMPACT. Every projectile stopped lights the lattice locally and sends a ripple
outward across the pane from the hit point, and the pane's overall opacity falls as `wallHP`
drains — so a barrier about to fail is visibly thinner. Same readability rule as
`guardian_light`, and it is the reason both spells feel like resources rather than timers.

Expiry dissolves from the ends inward. Destruction shatters. `IDestructibleObstacle` is the seam
— a `Health` on a Building-layer object is unreachable code, because every damage path finds its
victims through a `LayerMask` and a blocking wall must be on Building to block at all. The ice
wall shipped with `Health(100)`, a hit flash and a destruction sound that nothing in the project
could ever trigger.
