| 27 | `arcane_barrier` | arcane | Wall | Protection | free | 2 / 16 |

By role: Damage 8, Control 7, Protection 5, Mobility 3, Healing 2, Summon 2.
By cost: eleven are free or nearly so, four ride on S1, four on S2, and the remaining eight each
carry one system.

## New `SpellDefinition` fields

All appended, none inserted, every one defaulting to today's behaviour so no shipped asset
changes meaning.

```csharp
[Header("Buff")]
public StatModifier[] statModifiers;   // S1
public string buffKey;                 // S1 — blank falls back to spellKey

[Header("Projectile mechanics")]
public int   pierceCount;              // S2 — 0 = stop at first hit (today)
public float pierceDamageFalloff;      // S2 — fraction lost per body
public float homingStrength;           // S2 — deg/s, 0 = straight (today)
public float homingRange;              // S2 — acquisition radius, world units
public int   projectileCount = 1;      // S2
public float spreadDegrees;            // S2 — total fan across projectileCount

[Header("Charge")]
public float chargeMaxSeconds;         // S3 — 0 = not chargeable (today)
public float chargeMinFraction;        // S3
public float chargeDamageMultiplier;   // S3 — at full charge
public float chargeScaleMultiplier;    // S3 — at full charge
```

## New enum values — append only

- `SpellType.Buff` — after `EnergyCharge`. **Also add it to `CastFlourishProfile`'s switch under
  `Ward`**, or a self-buff falls through to `Hurl` and throws motes forward at nothing.
- `StatusEffectKind.Vulnerable` — after `Root`. Needed by S7.
- `StatusEffectKind.Marked` — after `Vulnerable`. Needed by `raise_thrall`.
- `SpellRole` — a new enum for S0.

Every one of these is serialised as an integer by shipped assets. Renumbering repoints authored
data at the wrong value without touching a file, silently.

## Every one of the 27 must author these

Fields that are load-bearing and are routinely left at a default that quietly means something
else:

- **`range`** — `Projectile.range` defaults to **20** and has silently truncated two spells
  already (the boomerang lost its entire return leg; the firework lost its whole flight).
- **`particleColor`** — opaque white is the "unauthored" sentinel (L10). Ten shipped spells are
  still in that state; do not add to them.
- **`element`** — an empty element falls through `MapSpellKeyToElement`, a legacy switch whose
  own comment tells new spells not to grow it. `fireball` gathered arcane violet for the life of
  the project because of this. Note that setting `element` also feeds `Health.MitigateDamage`, so
  it couples the spell to that resistance — `scatter_volley` deliberately leaves it empty because
  steel is not an element.
- **`cooldownDuration` > `duration`** for any persistent field with `maxInstances: 1`. Recorded
  three times (both vortices, `arcane_flame`). Applies here to `blizzard`, `static_field`,
  `cinder_trail`, `sanctuary`.
- **World units everywhere.** L11, five prior sightings.

## Fields to NOT reach for

`allowMovement`, `interruptible`, `lockCastDirection` and `allowOverlap` have **zero readers**
outside the F4 editor and the inspector. They are authored, round-tripped and inert — the same
family as `animation_map.json` and the FSM's `Actions` block. Do not tune behaviour through
them; if one of the 27 needs "cannot move while casting", that is new code, not a checkbox.

`SpellType.Trap` (8) and `SpellType.Shield` (9) are absent from the dispatch table and fall
through to `ProjectileExecutor` with a warning. Do not author against either.

## Tests that must go green

The project's recorded failure mode is authored-and-inert content — data that round-trips
perfectly and reaches no runtime code, recorded eleven times. Each of these tests exists to stop
one specific instance of that:

1. **`ShippedGrimoireCoverageTests`** (exists) — every player-castable spell belongs to exactly
   one school. Extend to the 27; it is what catches a spell that ships and cannot be learned.
2. **Every new `SpellDefinition` field has a reader.** A source scan asserting each of the twelve
   fields above is read by an executor or controller. This is the direct analogue of
   `PlayerStatsWiringTests`, which walks `StatKind` against its consumers for the same reason.
3. **`SpellRole` is set on every node.** A default-valued role tag is worse than no tag.
4. **Cooldown exceeds duration** for every `maxInstances: 1` persistent field.
   `VortexFieldTests` already does this for one spell; generalise it.
5. **World-unit sanity.** No shipped spell has a `radius`, `range`, `wallWidth`, `wallHeight`,
   `coneLength` or `distance` above 20 — the camera is 33 u wide, so anything larger is a pixel
   value that escaped. This is the cheap test that would have caught all five prior sightings.
6. **Flourish family coverage.** Every `SpellType` resolves to a family other than the `Hurl`
   fallback unless it is genuinely a hurl. Catches a new type added to the enum and not to the
   switch.
7. **Additive alpha budget.** For each new rig, the summed alpha at the centre stays under about
   3 (L2). Measurable live through `execute_code`, the way the vortex's was.
8. **Composition, not halves.** `SPAWNER_COORDINATE_SPACE_DRIFT` and the boomerang audit both
   record that a test exercising one half of a pair proves nothing. For these 27 that means:
   fly the whole piercing shot and count the bodies; charge, release and measure the delivered
   damage; mark a target, kill it, and assert a thrall exists.

## Build order

Six stages. Each ends with playable content, which is the property that makes it safe to stop.

**Stage 1 — foundations (no new spells).** S0 (`SpellNode.role` + grimoire filter) and the
`SpellDefinition` field additions with their enum appends. Nothing visible ships; everything
after this is cheaper.

**Stage 2 — the eleven free spells.** `frost_nova`, `glacial_step`, `blizzard`, `thorn_burst`,
`entangle`, `spore_cloud`, `radiant_burst`, `thunderclap`, `arcane_barrier`, plus `shadow_step`
and `leap_slam` with their small additions. Pure authoring against executors that already work.
**Eleven new spells with no new systems** — this is the stage that proves the data model and it
should be done first even though it is not the most interesting work.

**Stage 3 — S1, the BuffExecutor.** Four spells (`frozen_ward`, `barkskin`, `blessing`,
`war_cry`) and, more importantly, the whole support category becomes data for the run to 100.

**Stage 4 — S2, projectile mechanics.** Four spells (`ice_lance`, `void_lance`, `seeking_shard`,
`scatter_volley`) and the option to retrofit any of the twelve existing projectiles.

**Stage 5 — the singles.** S4 `sanctuary`, S5 `static_field`, S6 `guardian_light`, S7
`curse_of_frailty`, plus `cinder_trail`. Independent of each other, so they can go in any order
or in parallel.

**Stage 6 — S3 and S8.** `charged_bolt` and the two summons (`summon_wolf`, `raise_thrall`).
Last because they are the largest, and safe to be last because everything above ships without
them.

If the work has to stop early, stopping after Stage 4 delivers **19 of the 27** and the two
mechanics that pay forward the most.

## The honest cost note

Three claims in earlier planning for this expansion were wrong and are corrected here, because
they were the basis of a cheaper-looking plan:

- The three summon spells were tagged "pure data". They are not — `SummonExecutor` produces a
  green circle with no AI, so every summon in the game is gated on S8, the largest item in the
  list. Two summons survive into the 27 (down from three) for this reason, and both sit in the
  final stage.
- `sanctuary` was tagged free. `TotemController` heals only its owner, so it needs S4.
- `arcane_turret` (a totem that shoots) and the corpse-raising version of `raise_thrall` were
  both cut. The turret needs target acquisition on a controller that has never had a notion of an
  enemy; the corpse version needed a death registry that does not exist. The mark-the-living
  redesign above replaces the second one and is strictly cheaper, because the hook lands while
  the entity is still alive and fully configured.

# Part 5 — What was deferred, and why

Recorded here rather than left for someone to discover.

## `guardian_light` has its pool but not its cracks

Part 3 specifies three coupled readings for the absorb shell: facet OPACITY falling with the
pool, hairline CRACKS accumulating a quarter at a time, and the colour cooling from gold toward
white. What shipped is the pool itself (`ShieldController.AbsorbPool`, drained on
`Health.OnDamageBlocked`), the break on the frame the pool empties rather than on its own clock,
and a ripple whose strength is scaled by the BITE each hit takes out of what is LEFT — so the
same blow rings the shell harder as the pool empties and the last hit before the break is the
loudest.

That last one is doing most of the work the three readings were meant to do together, which is
why the rest could wait. Adding the others means teaching `ShieldSphereFX` an integrity scalar
and threading it through `UpdateFacets` and `UpdateRim`; the class is four partials and its
alpha budget is tuned, so it is a real change rather than a constant.

## The animation state for the new spells is the default

None of the 27 authors `animState`, so each falls through the existing rule — Attack for the
two `usesAttackAnimation` spells (`scatter_volley`, `leap_slam`) and Cast for the rest. That is
correct but generic: `war_cry` in particular wants a shout pose rather than a conjuring, and
`leap_slam` wants the dwarf's charge variant. Those are `CastVariant.spellKeys` reservations on
the character, not spell data, so they belong in a player-art pass.

## No icons

`iconSprite` is empty on all 27. `Valkur > Spells > Assign Icons` is the existing tool; the
expansion ships without art rather than with placeholder art, because a wrong icon is worse than
a missing one in a picker.

## The five schools' masteries were not rebalanced

The 27 new nodes carry modifiers chosen to fit the existing curve, but the whole grimoire's
mastery budget has not been re-examined now that it is 71 nodes rather than 44. That is a
balance pass over shipped data, and it wants a play session rather than a table.
